newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes slightly down, late local buying.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes slightly down, late local buying.

text.p: IPE September Brent crude ended a few cents lower on Monday after some late selling brought the contract into the negative arena. In the last half hour of trade light buying from locals saw September touch $18.13 but the contract closed for the day down three cents at $18.09 a barrel.

News from the U.N. earlier on Monday that Iraq had submitted a new aid distribution plan, the terms of which have been agreed with U.N. officials, to U.N. headquarters in New York saw little price reaction.

Completion of the new aid distribution plan was a condition Iraq insisted be met before the resumption of crude exports. Western diplomats said last week that it will take around a week for the U.N. to review and approve the plan. The market estimated that Iraq would need to sell 1.5 million barrels of crude per day to meet its $1 billion limit by September. The start date for the second phase of the oil-for-food deal was June 8.

Traders were somewhat surprised that more downward pressure was not seen on the outright price. Many felt that the possibility of Iraqi crude exports resuming in the coming weeks was partly included in the current price. They still expected that news of a date for the start of exports or an indication of the volume the Iraqis would export on a daily basis would push prices lower.
"I think we will see $17.50 (September Brent) - perhaps a sharper fall on the snap (news) and gradually creep back up to steady around $17.50," one crude oil trader said.

Brokers said strength in the physical North Sea market was also price supportive at the front end. A cargo of early August Brent crude oil traded on Monday at August Brent +5 cents - up ten cents from a deal on Friday.
